description: The factory that creates short-lived `HttpClient` instances over pooled, periodically recycled message handlers, avoiding both socket exhaustion and stale DNS.
A class registered with `AddHttpClient<T>` that receives a configured `HttpClient` in its constructor, is registered as transient and wraps one external API.
Outgoing HTTP middleware that wraps the next handler, registered as transient and added with `AddHttpMessageHandler<T>()`.
`AddStandardResilienceHandler()` adds a rate limiter, a 30-second total timeout, three retries, a circuit breaker and a 10-second attempt timeout to a client.
A strategy that stops calling a failing dependency for a break period once the failure ratio crosses a threshold, so callers fail fast instead of piling up.
Retrying a request with side effects such as `POST`, which can duplicate work unless the endpoint is idempotent; `DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods()` switches it off.
How long the factory reuses a message handler before recycling it, two minutes by default and set with `SetHandlerLifetime`.
